record.program_name: Homeless Housing, Assistance and Prevention (HHAP) Rounds 1 to 7 and other CoC-administered funds, Merced City and County CoC CA-520
record.administering_agency: Merced County Human Services Agency (Collaborative Applicant and Administrative Entity for the Merced City and County Continuum of Care; collabapp@countyofmerced.com)
record.typical_award_size: HHAP-6 allocations: Merced County $955,092.45 and Merced County CoC $1,020,055.16; HHAP-7 preliminary: County $915,168.72, CoC $980,537.91. CoC-administered rounds: HHAP-1 $716,227.19, HHAP-2 $338,893 (rapid rehousing $171,115, D Street Shelter operating subsidy $100,000, HMIS and CES $16,944), HHAP-3 $909,988.45, HHAP-4 $1,136,537.22 ($400,000 unobligated at reporting); the CoC also managed HHIP $1,260,500, ESG $2,452,084, ESG-CV $3,170,800, HEAP $1,338,104.53, CESH $1,637,863 and HUD CoC grants $6,433,137, a total of $19,950,660.47 across 14 sources from FY 2016-17 to FY 2023-24. The state dashboard reports $4 million of HHAP rounds 1 to 5 went directly to Merced County.
record.affordability_requirement: Homeless and at-risk households; 10% youth set-aside; Coordinated Entry referrals; 2024 Regionally Coordinated Homelessness Action Plan with the City of Merced.
record.next_deadline: No local capital NOFA; the CoC's 2024 regional plan lists CDBG, HOME, Homekey, PLHA, MHP and REAP as sources it will pursue for dedicated affordable units, led by local jurisdictions. HHAP-7 allocations are preliminary for FY 2026-27.
record.layering_notes: Merced County has no County housing finance program: the Community and Economic Development Department handles planning and the Housing Element, the Human Services Agency is Collaborative Applicant and Administrative Entity for the Merced City and County Continuum of Care (CA-520) and HHAP, Behavioral Health and Recovery Services holds BHSA, and the Housing Authority of the County of Merced (HACM) is the countywide PHA. The County is a non-entitlement jurisdiction for CDBG and HOME, has no housing trust fund, inclusionary ordinance, in-lieu fee or fee waiver, and Measure V (MCAG half-cent sales tax) is transportation only. The City of Merced is the entitlement jurisdiction with PLHA and Homekey awards (Pass 3). countyofmerced.com is Cloudflare-blocked to automated access (pages, DocumentCenter and AgendaCenter), so records were built from HCD tables and letters, mercedcoc.org reports, merced-pha.com, gocodebook (County Code Title 18) and press coverage; County documents are flagged for confirmation. HHAP in Merced funds rapid rehousing and the D Street Shelter rather than capital; Homekey units in the region (1213 V Street, 95 units; R Street, 21 veteran PSH units) are City of Merced projects. A PSH developer should seek a CoC letter of support and Coordinated Entry referrals. Source is the Merced CoC Grants and Funding Report (FY 2016-17 to FY 2023-24) on mercedcoc.org; HHAP-6 and HHAP-7 figures from HCD allocation tables.
eligible_project_detail: dedicated affordable housing units with rapid rehousing assistance (regional plan action 1a.3)

record.program_name: County exempt surplus land declarations (2490 Emma Street, Snelling; Castle Commerce Center, Atwater)
record.administering_agency: Merced County Executive Office and Department of Public Works (Castle)
record.typical_award_size: Castle Commerce Center: the Board adopted Resolution 2026-46 (agenda item 19, July 14, 2026) declaring 2045 Stratofortress Drive, Atwater (APN 051-010-058, about 43,500 sq ft) exempt surplus land under Gov. Code 54221(f)(1)(Q). The parcel is public-use airport land where FAA Order 5190.6B prohibits residential uses, and it is to be sold at fair market value for compatible airport commercial use (notice July 17, 2026). 2490 Emma Street, Snelling, was also reported as an exempt declaration with an August 27 to September 17, 2026 review window, but the County document was no longer online and that was not re-verified.
record.affordability_requirement: Surplus Land Act: non-exempt dispositions give affordable housing developers priority and require 25% lower income units for 55 years; exempt declarations avoid that process.
record.next_deadline: Monitor HCD's surplus land notice list and the County's Declaration of Exempt Surplus Land pages; respond within the 30-day review windows.

record.audit_note: The original Declaration of Exempt Surplus Land page (/4455) returns 404. Castle Commerce Center airport parcels cannot be used for housing, which contradicts the earlier workforce housing note. Monitor HCD's Surplus Land Act notice portal for any non-exempt County dispositions.

record.program_name: Atwater Housing Successor to the former Atwater Redevelopment Agency (Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Fund)
record.administering_agency: City of Atwater as Housing and Non-Housing Successor Agency
record.typical_award_size: Unknown. The City elected to be the housing successor, but the successor agency page lists only 2012-2015 ROPS and oversight board documents. No current SB 341 report or fund balance was found.
record.layering_notes: Recorded so the asset fund is not missed. The page lists no housing awards or reports, so do not assume any cash. Ask the City for its latest SB 341 report and any housing successor-owned parcels. atwater.org opened directly; a site search for 'housing successor' returned no reports.
record.audit_note: The Atwater successor agency page still lists only 2012-2015 ROPS and oversight board documents, a web search found no Atwater SB 341 housing successor report, and no program guideline states a prevailing wage rule, so award size and prevailing wage stay unknown.
